title: Repaint the fence
prompt:
Each character of planks is a plank's paint colour; repaint at most k planks and return the length of the longest contiguous run you can make that is all one colour.

- planks has 0 to 100,000 uppercase English letters; 0 <= k <= len(planks).
- A repaint changes one plank to any colour.
- Return an integer.
hints: A window can be made uniform when its length minus the count of its most common colour is at most k.
Grow a window to the right with letter counts; when it becomes invalid, slide the left edge forward by one.
Track maxCount, the largest count ever seen in a window. It never needs to decrease: the answer only improves when a window holds a higher count, so the window length never has to shrink.

solution.py:
def longest_repaint_run(planks, k):
    counts = [0] * 26
    left = 0
    max_count = 0
    for r, ch in enumerate(planks):
        c = ord(ch) - 65
        counts[c] += 1
        max_count = max(max_count, counts[c])
        if r - left + 1 - max_count > k:
            counts[ord(planks[left]) - 65] -= 1
            left += 1
    return len(planks) - left
solution.explanation: The window never shrinks: it grows when valid and slides (left and right both advance) when not, so its length is the best seen so far, and the answer is n - left at the end. A stale maxCount can only keep the window at its current size, never grow it wrongly, because growth needs a genuinely larger count.

complexity.notes: Counts are a fixed 26-entry array. Recomputing the exact max over 26 letters each step also works in O(26n).

followUps: Solve it by trying each target colour separately with a simpler window. What does that cost?
Return the start index of the best run as well, choosing the leftmost on ties.
